limit_or_fact: Adults: less than 5 g salt a day (under 2,000 mg sodium), just under a teaspoon
effect_as_source_states: High sodium mainly raises blood pressure; raised blood pressure is linked to heart disease, stroke and kidney disease
safe_reel_wording: Too much salt raises blood pressure, which is linked to heart and kidney disease (WHO)

limit_or_fact: Adults and children: free sugars under 10% of daily energy; under 5% (about 25 g, 6 teaspoons) for extra benefit
effect_as_source_states: Linked to weight gain and tooth decay
safe_reel_wording: Keep added sugar low: WHO says under 10% of calories, ideally about 6 teaspoons a day

limit_or_fact: Added sugar under 5% of daily calories (over age 2); no added sugar for children under 2
safe_reel_wording: ICMR-NIN: keep added sugar under 5% of calories; none for babies under 2

limit_or_fact: Research reviews link high added sugar/fructose intake to fatty liver (NAFLD)
effect_as_source_states: Research association, not a cure/cause claim for any product
safe_reel_wording: Studies link a high-sugar diet to fatty liver; say 'linked to', never 'causes' or 'damages'

limit_or_fact: Minimise ultra-processed foods high in fat, sugar and salt; read labels
safe_reel_wording: Cook fresh, limit packaged snacks high in salt, sugar and fat (ICMR-NIN)

limit_or_fact: Caution against prolonged use of protein powders and high-protein concentrates
effect_as_source_states: ICMR advises getting protein from food
safe_reel_wording: Get protein from food first: dal, eggs, meat, seeds (ICMR-NIN)

limit_or_fact: Labels must declare: gluten cereals (wheat, rye, barley, oats), crustaceans, milk, eggs, fish, groundnuts and tree nuts, soybeans, sulphites (10 mg/kg+)
safe_reel_wording: Allergic? Indian labels must declare 8 allergen groups: check before you buy
